subject: ventures/shop-rate-calculator
professional: a CFO / outsourced accountant for small trade contractors (HVAC, plumbing, electrical service shops) who builds their labor-burden and overhead-recovery models. First checks: is burden spread over billable (not paid) hours, is overhead allocated on a base that the pricing actually recovers it from, is target margin applied on price not cost, and does the hourly rate plus the material pricing policy actually yield the target net margin on the year.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python recomputation (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/c7304b9d-df3b-5ee4-a22c-4f77dc61075f/scratchpad/shoprate_indep.py) from standard practice (annual employment cost over billable hours; overhead / annual direct cost; price = cost/(1-margin)) against the engine (node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/c7304b9d-df3b-5ee4-a22c-4f77dc61075f/scratchpad/shoprate_tool.mjs calling calculateShopRate) on the shipped example: billable 1,568 h, cost/billable h 53.76, burden 91.98%, overhead 21.25% of direct cost, break-even 65.18, bill rate 74.07 -- all identical. Current-rate comparison at $70: margin 6.89%, gap -4.07/h, annual gap -19,137, required 1,659 h (79.8%) -- identical. Margin-vs-markup identity: 74.07 gives exactly 12.00% on price (13.64% markup-equivalent). what-should page's sensitivity claim (65% billable -> break-even ~$76) recomputes to 75.59. Blank, whitespace, '1,200', 'abc' are rejected; '-5' rejected; '1e3' accepted as 1000 (harmless). The arithmetic is right; held at 3 not 4 because the headline rate only produces the target net margin under an unstated ~37.8% markup on materials (see domain/fitness), and payroll tax is a flat % of all wages with a 10% default where FICA 7.65% + FUTA 0.6% on $7,000 + SUTA on a capped base gives 8.0-9.2% at a $58,240 wage.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked by run or code: burden per billable hour (works), overhead on direct cost (works), break-even and target bill rate (works), annual year view (works), current-rate comparison with margin/gap/required hours and unreachable branch (works; 30-week seasonal year also computes), carry to portfolio-shop-rates with merge/no-clamp/ceiling warnings (shop-rates.test.mjs reads platform/pages/rates.mjs; passes), save/forget scenario locally (page.test.mjs), usage tally with DNT/GPC/opt-out (usage.test.mjs), four content pages linked from llms.txt and sitemap. 108 venture index.html files carry a burdenRate/burdenPercent field, backing '100+ calculators'. No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/shop-rate-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 104/104 pass, 0.26 s. Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py on calc.mjs: days-off hours fixed at 8/day caught; materials dropped from direct-cost denominator caught; margin as markup (x1.12 instead of /0.88) caught; overhead double-applied in required-hours inversion caught; reachable ceiling workedHours -> paidHoursPerYear SURVIVED; burden note threshold >= 60 -> > 60 SURVIVED. 4 of 6 caught; both survivors are boundary conditions, one of which (the 'no schedule saves the rate' verdict) is a user-visible message. page.test.mjs is regex-on-HTML, so prose claims like the markup example are not checked.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (462 lines), shop-rates.mjs (145), index.html form and script sections, page.test.mjs headers. Pure engine, blank-is-error validation, explicit workedHours<=0 and billable<=0 guards, storage access wrapped against SecurityError, contract with platform/pages/rates.mjs pinned by a test that reads that file. Minor: the vs-housecall-pro/vs-servicetitan disclaimers mention 'fire-safety advice' and 'submitting a bid', boilerplate copied from another venture; README files table and privacy section predate the saved-scenario feature.
evidence.claims: Checked against files and recomputation: README/what-should/FAQ figures 53.76, 92%, 21.3%, 65.18, 74.07, 73.00/10.7%, 15% over revenue, $70 -> 6.9%/4.07/19,137/1,659 h (80%) all reproduce. FAIL: index.html:126 hint says 'a 10% mark-up on $10,000 of cost is $909' -- it is $1,000 of profit on an $11,000 price (9.1% margin); the site's own what-should page:96 states it correctly, so the main tool page contradicts the explainer on the exact concept it is teaching. PARTIAL: meta description and what-should page present 74.07 as 'the hourly rate a trade job has to be sold at' and show 'Revenue you need $596,436' beside it, but hours at 74.07 bring in only $348,417; the rest requires materials marked up ~37.8%, never stated. STALE: README:134 'deliberately no share link and no saved bid' while index.html:129 ships 'Save this scenario on this device'; README:140 usage events omit scenario_saved. vs-housecall-pro / vs-servicetitan: no prices invented, no unsupported feature claims, non-affiliation stated; fair. 'small crew commonly lands between $65 and $95' (what-should FAQ) has no cited source. Disclaimer present on every page. Served llms.txt clean (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs shop-rate-calculator: no placeholder origin).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job a contractor brings: enter payroll/overhead, get a rate, carry it. Carrying into the bid calculators works and is consistent, because those apply overheadRate to labor+materials (platform/pages/rates.mjs:172). But the standalone 'charge per hour' answer -- the search intent of what-should-i-charge-per-hour.html -- is unsafe for a time-and-materials shop: billing labor at the shown $74.07 with materials at cost nets 0.67% for the year, at +15% material markup 5.5%, at +20% 7.0%, versus the 12% target the page reports. The page never tells the user what material markup its rate assumes, nor offers the alternative of loading all overhead onto labor hours.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard contractor overhead-recovery practice (e.g. the labor-hour vs direct-cost allocation choice taught in construction cost accounting; burden incl. non-productive time). Burden over billable hours and margin on price are correct and well explained. Departures: (1) overhead allocated over labor+materials while the hourly 'shop rate' is presented alone, without the paired material markup (1+OH)/(1-m) = 1.378 -- a CFO would insist on either stating that markup or allocating overhead to labor hours for a T&M rate; (2) payroll taxes modelled as a flat % of all wages with no note that FUTA ($7,000) and SUTA wage bases cap them, and a 10% default above the 8.0-9.2% statutory range for the example wage; (3) workers' comp as % of all wages ignores that overtime premium and some payroll are excluded, acceptable given the 'use your declarations page' hint.

defects.what: The hourly bill rate is presented as what a job 'has to be sold at' for the target net margin, but overhead is allocated over labor+materials, so the target is only reached if materials and subs are marked up by (1+OH)/(1-m) (37.8% on the example). Billing labor at $74.07 with materials at cost nets 0.67%, not 12%. The page shows 'Revenue you need $596,436' beside the rate without saying that $248k of it must come from material markup.

Margin/markup hint states 'a 10% mark-up on $10,000 of cost is $909'; it is $1,000 of profit (9.1% margin). Contradicts the site's own explainer (what-should-i-charge-per-hour.html:96) on the very concept the hint teaches.

Payroll taxes are a flat % of all wages with a 10% default and no note that FUTA ($7,000) and SUTA wage bases cap the unemployment taxes; statutory employer taxes at the example's $58,240 wage are about 8.0-9.2%.
Two boundary conditions untested: the 'no schedule saves the rate' reachability ceiling (workedHours) and the >=60% burden note threshold both survive mutation.
README says there is 'deliberately no share link and no saved bid' and lists three usage events, but the page ships 'Save this scenario on this device' and counts scenario_saved.
Comparison-page disclaimers mention 'engineering, or fire-safety advice' and 'submitting a bid', boilerplate copied from another venture.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: every figure on the shipped example (53.76/h, 92% burden, 21.25% overhead on direct cost, 65.18 break-even, 74.07 at 12%, and the $70 comparison) reproduces exactly from first principles, tests pass 104/104 and caught 4 of 6 seeded mutants, and the comparison pages are fair to Housecall Pro and ServiceTitan. It misses the bar on claims: the main page's margin-vs-markup hint gives a wrong number ($909 for what is $1,000), and the headline 'rate a job has to be sold at' silently depends on a ~38% material markup the page never states, so a time-and-materials shop billing that rate with materials at cost nets under 1%. Carrying the rates into the site's bid calculators, which apply overhead to labor and materials, is consistent and is the tool's strongest use.
